scope: Ground, water and sea in-situ sensor networks and other in-situ measurement (not weather stations, balloons, aircraft or drones).
method: Licence wording read on official pages with the built-in browser; CORS probed with curl using an Origin header (Access-Control-Allow-Origin returned = browser fetch OK). Repo grepped for existing use.
verdict_rule: GREEN only for public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, ODbL or an explicit commercial-use statement, permanently free. Disclaimer-only, unstated, non-commercial or fee-for-commercial = GREY/RED.

sources.name: USGS Water Data APIs (OGC API: monitoring-locations, latest-continuous, continuous, daily, field-measurements, peaks)
sources.platform: Streamgages, lake/reservoir gages, groundwater wells, springs (USGS + cooperator agencies)
sources.measures: Stage (00065), discharge (00060), groundwater depth (72019), water temperature, specific conductance, annual peak flows
sources.density: ~13,000 real-time streamgages; ~1M+ well sites with at least one field measurement; 15-min continuous values
sources.access: https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/v0/collections/{id}/items?bbox=..&f=json ; no key needed (optional free api.data.gov key raises rate limit)
sources.licence: "USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain."
sources.caveat: Some monitoring locations belong to cooperator agencies (agency_code e.g. MN040 Minnesota Geological Survey). For strict green, filter agency_code=USGS or check the cooperator's own terms.
sources.in_app: partly: web/app/points.js uses latest-field-measurements for well depth-to-water (param 72019). Streamgage stage/flood and peaks not used.
sources.usefulness: high (flood/basement/foundation): river stage vs flood stage near a home; groundwater rising = basement seepage, falling = clay shrink/foundation settling
sources.what_we_could_show: Gage dots on the globe coloured by current stage percentile; per-house 'nearest gage rose X ft this week'.

sources.name: USGS NWIS legacy WaterServices (iv / dv / gwlevels)
sources.platform: Same gages and wells as above
sources.measures: Instantaneous and daily values
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.caveat: Being retired in favour of api.waterdata.usgs.gov; build new work on the OGC API.
sources.usefulness: same as above; use only as fallback
sources.what_we_could_show: Fallback for the gage layer.

sources.name: USGS annual peak streamflow (OGC 'peaks' collection)
sources.platform: Streamgages
sources.measures: Annual maximum stage and discharge per water year, decades of record
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.usefulness: medium: flood history context for a neighbourhood ('river peaked at record level in 2024')
sources.what_we_could_show: Per-gage spark of annual peaks with the latest flood year highlighted.

sources.name: NOAA NWS National Water Prediction Service gauges (api.water.noaa.gov/nwps)
sources.platform: River forecast points (mostly USGS gages) with NWS flood categories
sources.measures: Observed + forecast stage, action/minor/moderate/major flood stage, flood impact statements
sources.licence: "The information on National Weather Service (NWS) Web pages are in the public domain, unless specifically noted otherwise, and may be used without charge for any lawful purpose"
sources.usefulness: high (storm/flood damage leads): which gages are at or above flood stage right now and what streets the NWS says flood at that stage
sources.what_we_could_show: Gage pins turning orange/red at minor/moderate/major flood stage, with the NWS impact text.

sources.name: USGS Flood Event Viewer / Short-Term Network (STN) high-water marks and storm-tide sensors
sources.platform: Surveyed high-water marks and temporary pressure sensors after floods/hurricanes
sources.measures: Peak water elevation at surveyed points (often on buildings), event-specific
sources.density: hundreds to thousands of HWMs per major event
sources.access: Old API https://stn.wim.usgs.gov/STNServices/*.json now 301-redirects to https://apps.usgs.gov/stnweb which returned 403 to automated access (2026-11-26). Event data releases also on ScienceBase.
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.caveat: Licence green; current machine access route unclear. Re-probe or use ScienceBase event data releases offline.
sources.usefulness: very high for storm/flood damage: an HWM is a measured flood height at a specific street location
sources.what_we_could_show: After a hurricane/flood, HWM points with water height above ground; homes inside the measured water surface flagged.

sources.name: USGS ComCat earthquakes (FDSN event web service + GeoJSON feeds)
sources.platform: ANSS seismometer networks
sources.measures: Earthquake location, depth, magnitude, time; also eventtype=landslide, quarry blast
sources.density: all US M~1+ (denser in CA/AK/WA), global M2.5+
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.in_app: archive only (archive/mpls/feeds.py; earthquake query url listed in web/app/catalog.js). Seismic design maps referenced in archive catalog.
sources.usefulness: medium: foundation/chimney/pool-crack leads after felt quakes
sources.what_we_could_show: Recent quake dots sized by magnitude, fading with age.

sources.name: USGS ShakeMap (ComCat product)
sources.platform: Seismometers + strong-motion stations + DYFI, interpolated
sources.measures: Gridded MMI intensity, PGA, PGV per event
sources.access: event detail GeoJSON -> products.shakemap[0].contents (cont_mmi.json, stationlist.json, grid.xml)
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS); contributed regional network station data distributed via USGS
sources.usefulness: high in quake regions: per-house modelled shaking intensity for foundation/masonry inspection leads
sources.what_we_could_show: MMI contour overlay; per-house 'shaking felt: MMI VI (strong)'.

sources.name: USGS Did You Feel It? (ComCat product)
sources.platform: Citizen reports aggregated by USGS
sources.measures: Community intensity per ZIP code and 1 km / 10 km geocoded cells, number of responses
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.usefulness: high: real reported shaking at 1 km, often mentions cracked plaster/chimneys
sources.what_we_could_show: 1 km cells coloured by reported intensity.

sources.name: EarthScope SAGE (ex-IRIS) seismic station metadata and waveforms (FDSN web services)
sources.platform: Broadband seismometers, strong-motion, infrasound
sources.measures: Raw ground motion waveforms; station locations
sources.licence: "all data originating from EarthScope operated facilities will be licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0)" ... "If data was previously released under a more restrictive license by a contributing data provider, that license still applies."
sources.caveat: Per-network: only EarthScope-operated or no-licence networks are CC BY; check the network's own licence for contributed networks.
sources.in_app: no (GNSS from same facility is in app)
sources.usefulness: low: raw waveforms are not per-house; ShakeMap/DYFI already distil them
sources.what_we_could_show: Station dots (CC BY attribution).

sources.name: EarthScope GAGE GNSS station velocities
sources.platform: Permanent GNSS stations
sources.measures: Horizontal/vertical ground motion mm/yr
sources.density: ~2,000 US stations, km to tens of km apart
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 ("allows anyone to use, share, adapt, and redistribute data for any purpose, including commercial applications")
sources.in_app: yes: usa/build_gnss.py -> web/app/data/gnss.json; used in web/app/points.js and usa/build_maintenance.py
sources.usefulness: medium: regional subsidence context for foundations
sources.what_we_could_show: Already shown.

sources.name: Strong-motion records: USGS NSMP via ComCat/ShakeMap; CESMD (CGS + USGS) portal
sources.platform: Accelerometers in free field and in buildings
sources.measures: Peak acceleration/velocity per station per event
sources.access: USGS NSMP values via ShakeMap stationlist.json (GREEN); CESMD https://www.strongmotioncenter.org
sources.licence: USGS-produced: US public domain. CESMD/California Geological Survey records: no explicit open licence found (state agency).
sources.verdict: GREEN (USGS NSMP via ShakeMap) / GREY (CESMD-only CGS records)
sources.usefulness: low beyond ShakeMap
sources.what_we_could_show: Station PGA labels inside the ShakeMap overlay.

sources.name: NOAA CO-OPS tide gauges / water levels (NWLON) + high-tide-flooding products
sources.platform: Coastal and Great Lakes water-level stations
sources.measures: 6-min water level, predictions, datums, sea-level trends, high tide flooding counts/outlooks, met sensors
sources.access: https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/prod/datagetter?... ; metadata https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/mdapi/prod/webapi/stations.json ; derived products API (dpapi) for HTF
sources.licence: "The information on government servers are in the public domain, unless specifically annotated otherwise, and may be used freely by the public."
sources.usefulness: high for coastal homes: king-tide/storm-surge flooding, sea-level trend at nearest gauge; seawall/dock/foundation corrosion leads
sources.what_we_could_show: Tide gauge pins with live water level vs flood thresholds; 'nearest gauge: sea level +X mm/yr, N high-tide flood days last year'.

sources.name: NOAA NDBC buoys and C-MAN stations
sources.platform: Moored buoys, coastal stations (plus partner stations relayed)
sources.measures: Waves, wind, pressure, water temperature
sources.licence: NOAA/NWS: "in the public domain ... may be used without charge for any lawful purpose" (NDBC disclaimer page redirects to the NWS disclaimer)
sources.caveat: Partner-owned stations (IOOS RAs, universities) relayed by NDBC may carry their own terms; restrict to NDBC-owned stations for strict green.
sources.usefulness: low-medium: storm wave height offshore preceding coastal damage
sources.what_we_could_show: Buoy dots with wave height during storms.

sources.name: Argo profiling floats (GDAC)
sources.platform: Autonomous ocean floats
sources.measures: Ocean temperature/salinity profiles 0-2000 m
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (SEANOE dataset licence link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
sources.usefulness: none for houses (globe eye-candy only)
sources.what_we_could_show: Fine dots in the ocean in dot-globe style.

sources.name: U.S. IOOS regional associations (ERDDAP, Sensor Map)
sources.platform: Regional buoys, shore stations, HF radar, gliders
sources.measures: Water level, waves, currents, water quality
sources.density: thousands of assets via regional portals
sources.access: https://erddap.ioos.us/erddap/ and each RA's ERDDAP; sensors.ioos.us
sources.licence: Per dataset ERDDAP 'license' attribute; many use the generic ERDDAP text (free use/redistribution, 'not intended for legal use') with no commercial statement; some from universities/private partners.
sources.caveat: Could become GREEN per dataset where the licence attribute is CC0/CC BY or the operator is NOAA.
sources.usefulness: low-medium
sources.what_we_could_show: Only datasets individually confirmed CC0/CC BY/federal.

sources.name: USDA NRCS SNOTEL and SCAN (AWDB REST API)
sources.platform: Automated snow (SNOTEL, ~900 western mountain sites) and soil climate (SCAN, ~200 sites) stations
sources.measures: Snow water equivalent, snow depth, soil moisture and soil temperature at 2-40 in depth, precip
sources.density: sparse (tens of km); SNOTEL mountains only
sources.licence: "Most information presented on the USDA Web site is considered public domain information. Public domain information may be freely distributed or copied, but use of appropriate byline/photo/image credits is requested."
sources.in_app: no (NRCS SSURGO soil is in app, not SNOTEL/SCAN)
sources.usefulness: medium: snow load for roofs in mountain towns; soil-moisture swings for foundations (sparse)
sources.what_we_could_show: Snow-water-equivalent dots; 'nearest SNOTEL: X in of water on the ground = roof load alert'.

sources.name: NOAA NOHRSC snow analyses and observed snowfall
sources.platform: Ground snow observations (co-op, CoCoRaHS-relayed, SNOTEL) assimilated into SNODAS
sources.measures: Snow depth, SWE (1 km SNODAS grid), daily observed snowfall point files
sources.density: 1 km grid; thousands of point obs
sources.licence: NOAA/NWS public domain ("may be used without charge for any lawful purpose")
sources.caveat: Point files may include CoCoRaHS observer reports; use the gridded NOAA product for strict green.
sources.usefulness: high for roof leads in snow states: per-house snow-water load estimate after storms (ice dams, collapse risk)
sources.what_we_could_show: Per-house 'snow load on roof ~X lb/sq ft' from the 1 km SWE grid.

sources.name: NOAA USCRN / USRCRN soil moisture and temperature
sources.platform: Climate reference stations with triplicate soil probes
sources.measures: Soil moisture and temperature at 5/10/20/50/100 cm, hourly
sources.licence: NOAA public domain
sources.usefulness: low (too sparse for per-house)
sources.what_we_could_show: Station dots with soil-moisture percentile.

sources.name: State mesonets' soil sensors (e.g. Oklahoma Mesonet, NY State Mesonet, others)
sources.platform: State/university station networks
sources.measures: Soil moisture/temperature at several depths
sources.licence: Oklahoma Mesonet: "Category 2: Commercial/Business Customers - Standard fees for data and data services apply"
sources.caveat: Check each state individually; none assumed green. Iowa Environmental Mesonet (already used for other feeds) is disclaimer-only.
sources.in_app: IEM used for weather feeds elsewhere (other lane)
sources.usefulness: would be medium
sources.what_we_could_show: Nothing until a state network publishes an open licence.

sources.name: U.S. Drought Monitor (NDMC / USDA / NOAA / NASA)
sources.platform: Expert synthesis of in-situ (streamflow, soil moisture, wells) + remote indicators
sources.measures: Weekly drought category D0-D4 polygons
sources.licence: "The U.S. Drought Monitor map and associated data are available and authorized for use by third parties, including by commercial and non-commercial entities. Credit must be properly attributed"
sources.caveat: Attribution text required: 'The U.S. Drought Monitor is jointly produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and NASA. Map courtesy of NDMC, via https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu.'
sources.usefulness: high: drought + expansive clay = foundation cracking; drought = irrigation/landscaping and pool-evaporation demand
sources.what_we_could_show: Weekly drought polygons; per-house 'in D2 Severe Drought for 9 weeks' combined with SSURGO shrink-swell.

sources.name: USGS landslide inventory, monitoring stations and ComCat landslide events
sources.platform: Field-mapped inventory + USGS slope monitoring sites (pore pressure, soil moisture, rainfall)
sources.measures: Landslide polygons/points; real-time hillslope sensors at a few sites
sources.density: inventory compiled from many sources; ~dozen monitoring sites
sources.access: US Landslide Inventory (USGS ScienceBase/ArcGIS); ComCat eventtype=landslide (CORS yes)
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS); some inventory records compiled from state surveys carry their own terms
sources.usefulness: medium in hilly regions: foundation/retaining wall/drainage leads
sources.what_we_could_show: Mapped landslide polygons near homes.

sources.name: USGS borehole extensometers (land subsidence/compaction) via Water Data
sources.platform: Extensometer wells (CA, AZ, TX, NV)
sources.measures: Aquifer-system compaction (land subsidence) time series
sources.access: api.waterdata.usgs.gov continuous/field-measurements by site; some as ScienceBase data releases
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.usefulness: low-medium (very few sites; pairs with GNSS already in app)
sources.what_we_could_show: Extensometer pins with cumulative compaction.

sources.name: USGS Geomagnetism observatories
sources.platform: 14 magnetic observatories
sources.measures: Magnetic field components (H,D,Z,F), 1-s/1-min
sources.licence: US public domain (USGS)
sources.usefulness: none for houses
sources.what_we_could_show: Skip.

sources.name: Water Quality Portal (USGS NWIS + EPA WQX)
sources.platform: Sampled wells, streams, lakes from USGS, EPA, states, tribes, volunteers
sources.measures: Lab results: nitrate, arsenic, hardness, chloride, bacteria, PFAS etc.
sources.density: millions of sites; wells dense in places
sources.licence: No licence statement on the portal pages read (home, FAQs). NWIS-provider records are USGS public domain; WQX records come from states/tribes/volunteer groups with no stated licence.
sources.usefulness: medium for plumbing/water-treatment leads: hard water (scale on fixtures/water heaters), high chloride (corrosion) in groundwater
sources.what_we_could_show: USGS-sampled well dots coloured by hardness; 'local groundwater is very hard (X mg/L CaCO3)'.

sources.name: EPA RadNet
sources.platform: ~140 fixed air monitors + precipitation/drinking water sampling
sources.measures: Gamma radiation, beta in air
sources.licence: EPA disclaimer: "These documents may be freely distributed and used for non-commercial, scientific and educational purposes. Commercial use of the documents available from the EPA websites may be protected under the U.S. and Foreign Copyright Laws." (geospatial data produced by EPA stated as public domain)
sources.caveat: Federal work is PD by statute, but EPA's own wording hedges commercial use; also not house-relevant. Note: EPA radon zone maps are a separate (atmosphere/geology) item.
sources.usefulness: none
sources.what_we_could_show: Skip.

sources.name: ALERTWildfire / ALERTCalifornia cameras
sources.platform: Mountaintop PTZ cameras
sources.measures: Live images for fire detection
sources.access: https://www.alertwildfire.org/ (web viewer; login for some features)
sources.licence: No licence or reuse terms published on the site (only a cookie policy); About page only gives contact information.
sources.usefulness: low (images, not parcel data)
sources.what_we_could_show: Nothing; link out only.

sources.name: Citizen-science species records: GBIF (incl. iNaturalist research-grade) filtered to CC0/CC BY
sources.platform: Smartphone observations
sources.measures: Species occurrences (termites, carpenter ants, invasive plants, tree pests)
sources.licence: Per record: CC0, CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-NC 4.0. Only CC0/CC BY qualify. iNaturalist API terms page was behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read; prefer GBIF route.
sources.verdict: GREEN (CC0/CC BY records via GBIF) / RED (CC BY-NC records)
sources.in_app: listed in web/app/catalog.js (CC0/CC BY ready; CC BY-NC excluded)
sources.usefulness: medium: termite (Reticulitermes, Coptotermes formosanus) and emerald ash borer sightings near homes -> wood damage / tree removal leads
sources.what_we_could_show: Termite/ash-borer sighting dots within 1 km of a house.

sources.name: eBird (Cornell Lab)
sources.platform: Citizen bird checklists
sources.measures: Bird observations
sources.licence: "You will not use the API or API Content, either whole or in part, for commercial purposes whatsoever without prior written permission"
sources.usefulness: none
sources.what_we_could_show: Excluded.

sources.name: NASA GLOBE Observer
sources.platform: Citizen app (clouds, mosquito habitats, land cover, trees)
sources.measures: Photos + observations
sources.licence: Not verified: no data-use statement found in the time available.
sources.usefulness: low
sources.what_we_could_show: Skip.

sources.name: Municipal IoT open data, e.g. Chicago Array of Things / Chicago Data Portal sensors
sources.platform: Street-pole sensor nodes, beach water sensors, etc.
sources.measures: Environment, noise, beach water quality
sources.licence: City of Chicago Data Terms of Use: "These Terms of Use do not grant anyone any title or right to any patent, copyright, trademark or other intellectual property rights that the City may have"; City "reserves the right to claim or seek to protect any ... copyright"
sources.caveat: Other cities differ; only use a city portal dataset whose metadata states PD/CC0/CC BY/ODbL.
sources.usefulness: low
sources.what_we_could_show: Skip unless a city publishes CC0.

sources.name: Noise monitoring networks (airport noise monitors, NYC SONYC etc.)
sources.platform: Fixed microphones
sources.measures: dB levels
sources.access: per operator; mostly vendor portals (e.g. airport WebTrak)
sources.licence: No open licence found; vendor-portal terms.
sources.caveat: BTS National Transportation Noise Map (modelled, federal PD) is a non-sensor alternative for another lane.
sources.usefulness: low
sources.what_we_could_show: Skip.

sources.name: EIA energy infrastructure and utility data
sources.platform: Utility reporting (not sensors)
sources.measures: Power plants, retail prices, RECS pool share
sources.licence: "U.S. government publications are in the public domain" (eia.gov/about/copyrights_reuse.php)
sources.in_app: yes (archive/mpls/infra.py, archive catalog: EIA-860M, RECS SWIMPOOL)
sources.usefulness: low-medium (already covered)
sources.what_we_could_show: Already in app.

sources.name: HIFLD Open
sources.platform: Federal infrastructure layers
sources.measures: n/a
sources.licence: discontinued; use each agency's own source
sources.usefulness: none
sources.what_we_could_show: Use agency sources instead.

sources.name: City building permits
sources.platform: Administrative records
sources.measures: Permits (roof, pool, plumbing)
sources.licence: per city (handled by other lanes)
sources.usefulness: high
sources.what_we_could_show: Already in app.

top_recommendations: noaa_nwps + usgs_waterdata_ogc streamgages: live flood-stage layer (CORS, PD)
usdm drought polygons x SSURGO shrink-swell: foundation-crack risk per house (explicit commercial OK)
usgs_dyfi + usgs_shakemap: per-house reported/modelled shaking after quakes (CORS, PD)
noaa_coops tide gauges + high-tide-flooding counts for coastal homes (CORS, PD)
noaa_nohrsc SNODAS SWE: roof snow-load per house in snow states (PD)
